statement: The recorded dose of 100 units of regular insulin is dangerously excessive for a blood sugar of 210 mg/dL and could cause life-threatening hypoglycemia; I will not administer this dose. A typical correction dose for this blood sugar level would be in the range of 2-8 units depending on the patient's insulin sensitivity factor. This order requires immediate clarification from the prescriber before any insulin is administered.
judge_text:
WRONG
The answer states "100 units of regular insulin is dangerously excessive... could cause life-threatening hypoglycemia" and gives the correct range of 2-8 units.
